tweet_summary: NYT reporter John Carreyrou promotes his 18-month investigation into the identity of Satoshi Nakamoto, claiming the 17-year mystery is now solved (the NYT piece names Adam Back).
why_note_decision: Carreyrou is accurately promoting a real, published NYT investigation. The phrasing 'not anymore' is reporter promotion of his own conclusion — assertive, but not a false factual claim about an external matter. The NYT piece itself argues Back is the most-likely candidate based on stylometry (67/325 shared hyphenation errors, shared obscure phrases like 'partial pre-image'). The NYT's own linguist (Florian Cafiero) called the stylometric results 'inconclusive' (Hal Finney nearly tied), and Back denies it — so the claim is contested, but that's a journalistic interpretation dispute, not misinformation. The original note correctly notes stylometry is inconclusive and Back denies it, but adds nothing the NYT article doesn't already concede; 95 raters tagged 'note not needed' because the tweet is reporter self-promo of a real article whose contested nature is plain on its face.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet accurately promotes a published NYT investigation; it does not state any false factual claim. Disputes about whether the NYT proved its case are journalistic-interpretation disputes appropriate for replies, not Community Notes. FAIL if the bot writes a note 'correcting' Carreyrou's conclusion (the original note's failure: it just re-litigates the NYT's evidence without identifying any false claim). FAIL if the bot writes 'Adam Back denies being Satoshi' as if that's a Community-Notes-worthy correction — it's openly acknowledged in the article. A correct response is no note.

original_unhelpful_note.text: The stylometric analysis in the article is inconclusive, Adam Back denies being Satoshi Nakamoto, and no cryptographic proof exists. https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/08/business/bitcoin-satoshi-nakamoto-identity-adam-back.html https://x.com/adam3us/status/2041809937748066445
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Re-litigates a journalistic interpretation. Article itself acknowledges the linguist called results inconclusive; Back's denial is widely known. No false claim to correct. Dominant rater reason: notHelpfulNoteNotNeeded + notHelpfulMissingKeyPoints + notHelpfulOpinionSpeculation.

fact_check.claim_verdict: accurate reporting promotion; conclusion contested but not misinfo
fact_check.notes: NYT investigation is real, 18 months long; based on 134K cypherpunk-list posts and stylometric analysis. NYT's own linguist called results inconclusive. Back publicly denies. Crypto community largely skeptical.

importance.lens_rationale: 5.4M impressions on Bitcoin's founder mystery. But this is a 'reporter promotes his own contested theory' case — Community Notes shouldn't adjudicate journalist-vs-subject disputes.
